name.description: The name of the logging sink. Must be unique within the folder and helps identify the purpose of the sink.
name.rationale: While the name itself doesn't impact security, proper naming conventions help with identification, management, and auditing of logging sinks.

folder.description: The folder to which this logging sink applies. This specifies the organizational scope where the sink will collect and export logs.
folder.rationale: Proper folder scoping ensures that logging sinks only collect logs from intended resources and don't inadvertently capture logs from unrelated parts of the organization.

destination.description: The destination where the logs will be exported. Supported destinations include Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, and Logging buckets. The sink's service account must have write permissions to the destination.
destination.rationale: The destination choice impacts log security, retention, and accessibility. Secure destinations with proper access controls are essential for protecting sensitive log data.

filter.description: The filter that determines which log entries are exported by this sink. Uses Google Cloud Logging's advanced filter language to specify criteria for log selection.
filter.rationale: Proper filtering ensures that only relevant logs are exported, reducing storage costs and ensuring critical security logs are captured without unnecessary noise.

description.description: A human-readable description explaining the purpose, scope, and configuration of this logging sink.
description.rationale: Clear documentation of sink purposes helps maintain audit trails, ensures proper configuration management, and aids in security investigations.
description.compliant: Exports all GCE instance warning and error logs to BigQuery for security analysis and compliance auditing

disabled.description: Whether the logging sink is disabled. If true, the sink will not export any logs.
disabled.rationale: Disabled sinks should be carefully monitored as they may indicate broken log collection pipelines or security monitoring gaps.

include_children.description: Whether to include logs from all child projects of the folder. If true, logs from child projects are also exported; otherwise only logs relating to the provided folder are included.
include_children.rationale: This setting determines the scope of log collection and impacts both cost and security monitoring coverage across the organizational hierarchy.

intercept_children.description: Whether this sink should intercept and match with sinks in child resources, except _Required sinks. This sink will be visible to child resources when listing sinks.
intercept_children.rationale: Intercepting child sinks can help centralize log management but may conflict with project-specific logging requirements if not properly coordinated.

bigquery_options.description: Configuration options for BigQuery destinations. Controls how log data is structured and stored in BigQuery tables.
bigquery_options.rationale: BigQuery configuration options impact query performance, cost efficiency, and data accessibility for log analysis and security investigations.

use_partitioned_tables.description: Whether to use BigQuery partitioned tables instead of date-sharded tables. Partitioned tables require special query syntax but offer better performance and cost management for large datasets.
use_partitioned_tables.rationale: This is primarily a performance and cost optimization feature that doesn't directly impact security, though it affects query efficiency for security investigations.

exclusions.description: List of exclusion rules that specify which log entries should be excluded from this sink, even if they match the sink's filter.
exclusions.rationale: Exclusions must be carefully configured to avoid inadvertently filtering out security-critical logs while reducing noise and storage costs.

name.description: The name of the exclusion rule. Must be unique within the sink.
name.rationale: Proper naming helps identify and manage exclusion rules, though the name itself doesn't impact security.

description.description: A description explaining why certain log entries are being excluded from the sink.
description.rationale: Documenting exclusion rationales helps maintain audit trails and ensures security teams understand why certain logs are being filtered out.
description.compliant: Excludes high-volume health check logs to reduce storage costs while maintaining security-relevant logging

filter.description: The filter that determines which log entries to exclude from the sink. Uses Google Cloud Logging's advanced filter language.
filter.rationale: Exclusion filters must be precise to avoid inadvertently filtering security-critical logs while reducing unnecessary log volume.

disabled.description: Whether the exclusion rule is disabled. If true, the exclusion filter is not applied.
disabled.rationale: Disabled exclusions should be monitored as they may indicate incomplete logging configuration or security controls.
